s.description: Evaluate sync patterns against universal principles: primitive-role fit, contract enforcement, idempotency and ordering, failure handling, observability, cache coherence, sync-backup separation, topology coherence. Platform-neutral.

scope.files_in_scope: Any source code, infrastructure-as-code, schema definitions, and sync-related specs in the target project.
scope.out_of_scope: Authentication, encryption-at-rest, general database design, frontend rendering. Defer to dedicated judges for these.

construct.statement: Sync quality is the degree to which a system's replication of state across boundaries is intentional, observable, schema-aware, recoverable, and architecturally distinct from backup. A sync architecture is well-designed when each flow uses a primitive whose properties match its requirements, validates contracts at every boundary, tolerates duplicate and out-of-order delivery, surfaces failures loudly, measures freshness, coheres caches, and treats backup as a separate concern.
construct.theory_of_quality: Sync failures are silent by default. They manifest as drift, duplicates, lost writes, stale reads, and split-brain — all of which look like "the app is slightly wrong" rather than "the system crashed." Quality therefore depends less on the absence of errors than on the presence of mechanisms that make errors detectable and recoverable. A judge measuring sync quality grades the mechanisms, not the absence of incidents.

universal_principles.principle: Every sync flow uses a primitive whose consistency model, latency profile, delivery guarantees, and durability properties match the flow's requirements. Property mismatch is the dominant cause of silent data loss in sync architectures.
Every sync boundary validates payload schema at runtime on both producer and consumer sides. Type-system claims at compile time are insufficient because sync crosses trust and version boundaries.

All sync mutations are safe to retry. Delivery semantics are declared per channel (at-least-once, at-most-once, exactly-once-via-dedup). Ordering guarantees are declared per channel (FIFO, causal, none).
Sync freshness is measured per flow. Lag is a first-class metric with an SLO. Stale state is detectable before it causes user-visible incorrectness.
Failures surface to operators and, where appropriate, consumers. Dead-letter paths exist for async channels. Poison messages neither silently drop nor permanently block.
Sync events trigger invalidation across every caching layer touched by the synced entity. Stale-after-write windows are declared and bounded.
Sync (current-state replication for freshness) and backup (point-in-time snapshots for durability) are architecturally separate. Replication is not backup. Conflation is a critical safety violation.

Sync decisions reference and cohere with state management and backup topology. Specs cross-reference. A sync flow that contradicts the state model or backup policy is a topology defect even if locally correct.

criterion.name: Primitive-Role Fit
criterion.S: Every flow's primitive selection justified against the primitive's declared property profile. Composition exceeds individual primitive limits in a documented way. Pattern reusable beyond this project.
criterion.A: Optimal primitive per flow with documented rationale citing consistency, latency, delivery, and durability properties.
criterion.B: Correct primitive per flow; rationale implicit but inferable from code.
criterion.C: Mostly correct; one or two sub-optimal choices that do not cause correctness violations.
criterion.D: Multiple property mismatches present, including at least one that risks user-visible incorrectness.
criterion.F: Critical mismatch: an eventually-consistent primitive used for transactional flow, a coordination primitive used for batch fan-out, or similar category error.

criterion.name: Contract Enforcement
criterion.S: Contracts auto-generated from a single source of truth; producer and consumer adapters derived from schema; shape mismatch architecturally impossible at runtime.
criterion.A: Contract-first design; producer and consumer both validate at runtime; breaking changes blocked in CI; versioning explicit.
criterion.B: Versioned contracts with runtime validation at every sync boundary.
criterion.C: Contracts exist; runtime enforcement has gaps at one or more boundaries.
criterion.D: Static types only; no runtime validation at sync boundary; relies on producer honesty.
criterion.F: No explicit contracts; payloads untyped or accepted without validation.

criterion.name: Idempotency and Ordering
criterion.S: Deterministic replay: any sequence of messages produces identical end state. Idempotency formally verified or property-tested.
criterion.A: Provably idempotent mutations; causal or FIFO ordering preserved where required; exactly-once semantics achieved via dedup plus idempotency keys.
criterion.B: All sync mutations idempotent; dedup tracked in persistent store; per-channel delivery semantics declared and handled.
criterion.C: Idempotency keys present on most paths; dedup tracked but with gaps.
criterion.D: Inconsistent idempotency handling; some channels missing keys; reliance on producer not retrying.
criterion.F: Replay produces duplicate writes or corrupted state. No idempotency mechanism.

criterion.name: Failure Handling
criterion.S: Adaptive failure handling: automatic rerouting, continuous chaos testing, zero manual intervention for known failure modes.
criterion.A: Self-healing: dead-letter reprocessing, split-brain detection, chaos-tested recovery paths, alerting on degradation.
criterion.B: Robust retry plus dead-letter plus alerting; reconnection recovers in-flight state.
criterion.C: Basic dead-letter and reconnect; some failure modes unhandled.
criterion.D: Retry exists but no dead-letter; poison messages block the consumer or are silently dropped.
criterion.F: Errors swallowed; no retry; no dead-letter; failures invisible to operators.

criterion.name: Sync Observability
criterion.S: Predictive: anomaly detection on lag patterns; sync health treated as SLI with error budget; auto-remediation triggered by SLO burn.
criterion.A: Real-time lag measurement; drift detection between systems; freshness SLO declared and tracked; automated remediation on violation.
criterion.B: Sync lag measured per flow via structured metrics; health checks; failure alerts wired to operators.
criterion.C: Some sync metrics exist but no explicit lag measurement.
criterion.D: Unstructured logging only; no structured metrics; sync health inferred manually.
criterion.F: No sync metrics; sync health entirely unknown until incident.

criterion.name: Cache Coherence
criterion.S: Cache invalidation derived automatically from sync events; zero per-entity invalidation config; sub-second freshness guaranteed and tested.
criterion.A: Sync-driven invalidation across every caching layer (persistent store, edge cache, client cache).
criterion.B: Comprehensive invalidation; sync events purge all dependent caches.
criterion.C: Most paths invalidate caches; edge cases produce stale reads.
criterion.D: Inconsistent invalidation across paths; stale reads possible on common paths.
criterion.F: Sync updates persistent store but caches remain stale indefinitely.

criterion.name: Sync-Backup Boundary
criterion.S: Unified data lifecycle: sync defined as freshness mechanism, backup defined as durability mechanism, transitions between them formally specified.
criterion.A: Explicit boundary with documented rationale; sync and backup tested independently with distinct failure scenarios.
criterion.B: sync-specs and backup-specs exist and cross-reference; clear conceptual separation.
criterion.C: Separate backup mechanism exists; boundary not documented.
criterion.D: Awareness of distinction present but not documented; relies on tribal knowledge.
criterion.F: Sync conflated with backup: replication treated as backup, or point-in-time recovery treated as sync.

criterion.name: Topology Coherence
criterion.S: Unified data architecture: sync, state, and backup specs are facets of one coherent model with consistent vocabulary and bidirectional traceability.
criterion.A: Integrated spec graph; sync decisions demonstrably informed by state model and backup topology.
criterion.B: sync-specs cross-references state-specs and backup-specs; primitive roles mapped consistently.
criterion.C: sync-specs exists but does not cross-reference adjacent specs.
criterion.D: Informal awareness of adjacent systems; no documentation.
criterion.F: Sync designed in isolation; contradicts state or backup decisions.

evidence_requirements.requirement: Every grade cites at least one of: a file path with line range, a spec section, or a documented absence (e.g. "no dead-letter binding found in any workflow definition under /sync").
Quotation preferred over summary. Paraphrase only when the original spans more than 10 lines.
Counter-evidence handling: when a flow shows mixed evidence, grade the weakest path and note the better paths in the rationale.
Absence of evidence equals grade D minimum on principles that require positive proof (idempotency, validation, observability, dead-letter).

bias_controls.control: A minimal correct architecture must not score lower than a verbose one of equal correctness. Word count and file count do not bear on grades.
Spec format (markdown, inline doc comments, JSON, YAML) does not affect grade if information content is equivalent.
The judge does not prefer specific named primitives or vendors. Primitives are evaluated only against their declared property profile relative to flow requirements.
The judge does not favor architectures that resemble its illustrative examples. Examples are non-grading.
Hedged correct findings outscore confident wrong ones. Cite evidence; do not assert.
A flow using older patterns scores equally to one using newer patterns if both satisfy the principle.

failure_modes.mode: Cannot evaluate runtime correctness; only structural evidence from code, schemas, and specs. A structurally sound architecture can still fail at runtime due to bugs the judge cannot see.
Cannot infer sync lag without observability data; absence of lag metrics is gradable, but actual lag is not.
Cannot fully evaluate chaos resilience without test results; relies on presence of chaos tests as proxy.
Cross-spec coherence requires specs to exist; absent specs grade D, not "inferred good from code."
Adversarial input: a project with verbose docs claiming features it does not implement can mislead absent code-level verification. The judge prefers code evidence over spec claims when they conflict.
Adversarial input: a project that defines its own custom "consistency" or "idempotency" terms differently from this judge's definitions. The judge uses its own definitions and notes the divergence.

process.step: Enumerate every cross-boundary state replication in the project. For each, record: source, destination, transport, consistency requirement, latency requirement, ordering requirement, durability requirement.
For each flow, identify the chosen primitive and compare its property profile to the flow's requirements. Flag mismatches by severity of property violated (correctness > performance > cost).
Apply SP1 through SP8 in order. For each principle, scan for positive evidence (mechanism present) and counter-evidence (mechanism absent where required).
Assign F-S with quoted or located evidence. Apply evidence_requirements rules. Apply bias_controls. If any control triggers, re-grade.

For every grade below B, emit a finding with severity, location, principle violated, and recommended remedy. Severity follows: SP1, SP2, SP3, SP5 violations are critical; SP4, SP6, SP7 are high; SP8 is medium.

Weighted composite. Critical criteria weighted 3, high weighted 2, medium weighted 1. Map S=5, A=4, B=3, C=2, D=1, F=0. Composite = sum(grade × weight) / max possible × 100. S-tier verdict requires composite ≥ 90 AND zero criterion below B.

If docs/sync-specs.md absent, create with the topology table, contract definitions, idempotency strategy, failure modes, observability map, and connected-system references. If present, update with any missing sections.

output_format.section: One paragraph restating what this evaluation measured for this specific project.
Table: flow name, source, destination, primitive, consistency need, latency need, delivery need.
For each C-* criterion: grade, evidence (quoted or located), brief rationale.
Severity-ranked list. Each finding: severity, principle, location, current state, target state, remedy.
Weighted score, tier (S/A/B/C/D/F), top three priority improvements, notes on any bias_controls triggered.

illustrative_examples.note: These examples are illustrative only. They do not bear on grades. They exist to disambiguate principles for raters unfamiliar with sync architecture vocabulary.
illustrative_examples.example: A "feature flag" system writes user-specific entitlement state to an eventually-consistent global config store with up to 60s propagation. The flow requires per-request correctness. The primitive's consistency profile does not match the flow's consistency requirement. This is an SP1 violation regardless of which vendor provides the eventually-consistent store.

A webhook consumer parses inbound JSON with a runtime schema validator (e.g. Zod, Ajv, Pydantic) before any side effect. Invalid payloads are routed to a dead-letter destination. The schema is versioned and shared with producers via a published artifact. This satisfies SP2.

A queue consumer increments a counter in the persistent store on every message. The queue offers at-least-once delivery. The consumer has no idempotency key check. Replay produces over-counting. This is an SP3 violation.

A WebSocket message handler wraps its body in try/catch and logs to stdout on failure, then returns normally. The error is invisible to operators and the message is acknowledged as processed. This is an SP5 violation.

An on-call runbook states "we are protected from data loss because our database has read replicas." Replication protects against replica failure, not against logical corruption, application bugs, or operator error. Treating replication as backup is an SP7 violation.

standardization_check.step: Inventory every sync flow; map each to source, destination, transport, and requirement profile
For each flow, compare chosen primitive's property profile to requirement profile; flag SP1 mismatches
Locate every sync boundary; verify runtime schema validation on both sides per SP2
For each mutation, verify idempotency key and persistent dedup tracking per SP3
For each async channel, verify dead-letter destination and alerting per SP5
For each flow, verify lag measurement with declared SLO per SP4
For each synced entity, verify cache invalidation cascade on write per SP6
Verify backup mechanism exists and is architecturally distinct from sync per SP7
Verify sync-specs cross-references state-specs and backup-specs per SP8
Apply bias_controls; if triggered, re-grade affected criteria
Emit findings with severity, location, principle, remedy
